title: How musicians reacted to Bird; who named bebop
summary: Most players said bebop was Chinese music because they could not play it; Grimes says he helped introduce Dizzy at the Apollo.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: How did other people react to Bird's music?

Oh yeah, it was knocke'd, it was nearly a strike. I mean, the guys, they couldn't play it see, cause they were still into Dixieland really, just out of Dixieland was Basie and Ellington, the way we played, and Eddie they went with Ben Webster. A few other groups even Stuff Smith & Eddie -- South. Even violin players was in it. Then

cats could play, not no gettin' around it. So it was. But they weren't into this new thing. 75% would speak against it. Say oh, man I don't know what they're playin' -- Chinese music. They'd call it everything. That's because they couldn't play it. It was out of their reach. Don Byas could reach it. He didn't have the tone, but he could play the notes -- he was in it. One of the few that I could remember. Somehow they finally hooked up, Parker and Diz, ... Al Haig used to play with me and I let him go overnight. I said, man, you fit right in there" ... And the other musicians just got jealous because they couldn't play. ...
When was the first time they used the term "Bebop"

... I think Diz named it himself ... I helped start him off ... as long as I have known him he never threw nothin' my way ... not once ... [shows picture] ... the thing of it is when he was making his debut, as you might say at the Apollo theater with his new modern music group, a few of us showed up to try to give him a send-off and there's a picture of myself, were on the Apollo theater stage ... bringing him on to introduce modern jazz -- Bebop -- to the public. That's me helpin' him out. But he's never thrown a thing my way or never mentioned my name or nothin' ...
